title: An-Naba': sleep as rest
hook: We made the earth a bed, mountains as pegs, sleep for rest, the night a cover (78:6–10)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the opening of An-Naba': about what are they asking? Your line was the great news.

Last night, at some point, you lay down, the thoughts slowed, and then, without deciding to, you were gone. Hours passed that you can't account for. Then you were back, the same person in the same bed, as if someone had pressed pause and then play. It happens every night, and it rarely gets a second thought. An-Naba' has named the great news, a Day when the dead are raised. Now it answers the doubters, and the answer surprises people. It doesn't argue at all. It points: at the ground under you, the mountains, your own pillow.
screen: `PAUSE, THEN PLAY.` → `EVERY NIGHT OF YOUR LIFE.` → `THE SURAH STOPS ARGUING AND POINTS.`

segments.voice: The surah asks a run of questions, and each one is a picture. Have We not made the earth a resting place, mihad, a word also used for a cradle or a spread bed? And the mountains as pegs, awtad, like the pegs that hold a tent down in the wind? And created you in pairs. Then the line for today: wa ja'alna nawmakum subata. And We made your sleep subat. The classical dictionaries tie subat to a root meaning to cut off, to stop, to rest; the same letters give sabt, the Sabbath. Sleep as the cutting off: the day's work and worry stop. Then the night as a garment, libas, the same word for clothing, wrapping you like a cover. And the day for earning a living. The argument is quiet but clear. You worry that raising the dead is impossible? You go through a small version every night. A verse in Surah az-Zumar says Allah takes the souls at the time of death, and takes those that have not died during their sleep, then keeps some and sends the others back until an appointed time. Muslim practice marks this at the edges of each night. At bedtime, Bukhari records, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ would say: in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live. And on waking: praise to Allah who gave us life after He had made us die, and to Him is the rising. Every morning, a rehearsal of the great news.
screen: `THE EARTH A BED, MOUNTAINS AS PEGS.` · `SUBAT — SLEEP AS THE CUTTING OFF.` · `THE NIGHT AS A GARMENT.` · `EVERY NIGHT, A SMALL RAISING.` · then, large: `SLEEP IS A SIGN.`

segments.voice: Sit or lie down, whichever your body wants, and let your eyes close. Starting at your feet, let each part go heavy, as if the earth really were a bed: legs, back, shoulders, jaw, each one done working for now, which is subat, the cutting off, in miniature. If you pray, you can say quietly, in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live, and then just rest.
An-Naba'. The great news, and the surah that answers it by pointing at the world: the earth a bed, the night a garment, and sleep made for rest. Today's word.
Your line: sleep is a sign. Your pillow is part of the argument. Sleep well tonight.

screen: `DAY 220 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: AN-NABA': THE DAY OF SORTING.`

howItsDone: Muslims who follow the Prophet's bedtime practice make wudu, lie on the right side, and say bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya (in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live), with a phrase of praise for being given life again on waking.

fork.setup: you're a doubter in Mecca, sure the dead can't rise. what does the surah point you to first?
options: the earth as a bed, the mountains as pegs, your own sleep
fork.reveal: 78:6–11 points at ordinary things: the ground, the mountains, pairs, sleep, night and day. the sign is the life you already live.

original.note: Arabic: rest, a cutting off (78:9, wa ja'alna nawmakum subata). the root also gives sabt, the Sabbath.

trapdoor: what you thought: a verse saying people need sleep.
what it means: sleep is one of a list of signs, a nightly small death and return that points to the raising.
what a scholar hears: subat from s-b-t, to cut off or rest; 39:42 pairs sleep with death; the Prophet's bedtime words, bismika amutu wa ahya.
